Institute Vision 
 “To attain perfection in providing Globally Competitive Quality Education to all our Students 
and also benefit the global community by using our strength in Research and Development” 
Institute Mission 
“To establish world class educational institutions in their respective domains, which shall be 
Centers of Excellence in their stated and implied sense. To achieve this objective we dedicate 
ourselves to meet the challenges of becoming Visionary and Realistic , Sensitive and 
Demanding, Innovative and Practical, Theoretical and Pragmatic; ALL at the same time” 
Department Vision 
To excel in the field of technical education and research by perseverance to produce high 
quality engineers and technologists having high levels of creativity and ethical standards, 
contributing effectively to the growth of our society and country 
Department Mission 
• To impart knowledge in the fields of Electronics, Communication and related areas 
with a focus on developing the necessary competencies, virtues and qualities expected 
of an electronics engineer by the society at large 
• To familiarize the students with the state of the art technology to meet the growing 
demands of modern industries 
• To foster self-development leading to positive social transformation 
 
Program Educational Objectives (PEOs) 
After successful completion of the program, the graduates will be able 
• To produce technically competent graduates with the ability to analyze, design, 
develop, optimize and implement electronic systems. 
• To excel in professional careers or pursue higher education by acquiring requisite 
knowledge in the field of Electronics and Communication Engineering. 
• To inculcate adaptability to current and changing trends by engaging in lifelong 
learning activities by research. 
 
Program Specific Outcomes (PSOs) 
At the end of the program, the student will be able to 
• Understand the concepts and applications in the field of Communication/networking, 
signal processing, embedded systems and semiconductor technology. 
• Design the analog and digital systems for given specifications and functions.

Engineering Mathematics-III 
Semester III CIE Marks 50 
Course Code 23BSEC201 SEE Marks 50 
Teaching Hrs/Week (L: T: P) 3:0:0 Exam Hrs 03 
Total Hrs 42 Credits 03 
Course Learning Objectives: This course is designed to 
1. Develop systematic understanding of Laplace transform and their applications in solving 
engineering and scientific problems 
2. Impart the knowledge of Fourier series and its applications in solving engineering problems  
3. Build a strong foundation in Fourier Transforms and Z-Transforms essential to solve real-world 
problems 
4. Provide a comprehensive understanding of Numerical Methods for solving problems arising in 
science and engineering 
Module 1: Laplace Transforms  No. of Hours: 09 
Laplace Transforms: Definition and Laplace Transform of elementary functions. Properties of 
Laplace Transform– Linearity, Shifting, Multiplication by 𝑡𝑛, Division by t , Unit-Step function, 
Dirac Delta function 
Inverse Laplace Transforms: Definition, Inverse Laplace Transform, Convolution theorem to find 
the inverse Laplace Transforms. Solution of differential equations using Laplace Transforms 
Module 2: Fourier Series No. of Hours: 08 
Introduction to Infinite series, Convergence and D ivergence. Periodic functions, Dirichlet’s 
condition. Fourier series of periodic f unctions with arbitrary period, Half range Fourier series , 
Practical Harmonic Analysis 
Module 3: Fourier Transforms and Z-Transforms No. of Hours: 09 
Fourier Transforms: Definition, Fourier Sine and Cosine transforms. Inverse Fourier Transforms, 
Inverse Fourier Cosine and Sine Transforms 
Z-Transforms: Definition, Standard Z-Transforms, Damping and Shifting rules. Inverse Z-
Transform and Applications to solve Difference Equations 
Module 4: Numerical Methods-I No. of Hours: 08 
Finite Differences, Newton’s Forward & Backward Difference, Newton’s Divided Difference, 
Lagrange’s and Inverse Lagrange’s Interpolation methods 
Module 5: Numerical Methods-II No. of Hours: 08 
Solution of Polynomial and Transcendental Equations: Regula-Falsi and Newton -Raphson 
methods 
Numerical Differentiation: Forward and Backward difference methods  
Numerical integration: Simpson's (1/3)rd rule, (3/8)th rule and Romberg’s method

Analog Electronic Circuits 
Semester III CIE Marks 50 
Course Code 23ECPC203 SEE Marks 50 
Teaching Hrs/Week (L: T: P) 3:0:0 Exam Hrs 03 
Total Hrs  42 Credits 03 
Course Learning Objectives: This course is designed to 
1. Familiarize the working principles of electronic devices like Bipolar Junction Transistors, Field 
Effect Transistor, power semiconductor devices 
2. Emphasize the design aspects of amplifiers using BJTs and FETs 
3. Impart skills to understand the oscillators and power amplifier circuits 
Module 1: BJT Biasing and AC model No. of Hrs: 10 
BJT Biasing: Base bias circuit, Emitter stabilized bias, Voltage divider bias, Collector feedback bias-
Design and Operation 
BJT AC Model: BJT modeling, The re-model, CE fixed bias, Voltage divider bias, Emitter follower, 
Darlington connection-DC biasing 
Module 2: Feedback Amplifier  No. of Hrs: 08 
Feedback Amplifier:   Feedback concept, Feedback connection types -Voltage series feedback, 
Voltage shunt feedback, Current series feedback and current shunt feedback amplifier, Input 
resistance, Output resistance and voltage gain of feedback amplifiers 
Module 3: Oscillators No. of Hrs: 08 
Oscillators:  Concept of positive feedback, Condition for sustained oscillation, Phase shift oscillator, 
Wien bridge oscillator, Tuned oscillator- Hartley and Colpitts oscillator, Crystal oscillators 
Module 4: Power Amplifiers No. of Hrs: 08 
Power Amplifiers: Amplifier types, Series fed Class -A amplifier, Transformer coupled Class A 
amplifier, Class B amplifier, operation and power calculations, Class C and Class D amplifiers 
Module 5: Field Effect Transistor and FET amplifiers No. of Hrs: 08 
Field Effect Transistor: Construction and characteristics of JFETs, MOSFETs -Depletion and 
Enhancement type 
FET Amplifiers: JFET small signal model, Fixed bias configuration, Self -bias and voltage divider 
configuration, Source follower configuration, Cascade configuration 
Course Outcomes: At the end of the course, the student will be able to 
1. Develop different biasing circuits for BJT and to analyze BJT AC model 
2. Describe different types of feedback amplifiers 
3. Design oscillators using transistors for different oscillating condition 
4. Identify different types of power amplifiers and construct them using BJT 
5. Explain the operation of Field effect transistor in amplifier application

Digital System Design using Verilog HDL 
Semester III CIE Marks 50 
Course Code 23ECPC204 SEE Marks 50 
Teaching Hrs/Week (L: T: P) 3:0:2 Exam Hrs 03 
Total Hrs  62 Credits 04 
Course Learning Objectives: This course is designed to  
1. Impart the knowledge of logic function minimization techniques and basic building blocks of digital 
circuits 
2. Enable design and analysis of combinational and synchronous sequential circuits 
3. Provide insights into design and implementation of digital circuits using HDL language 
Module 1: Introduction to Digital Circuits and HDL No. of Hrs: 10 + 02 
Introduction to Logic Circuits : Introduction to Boolean Algebra, Synthesis using gates, Design 
examples, Optimized implementation of logic functions, Karnaugh map: strategy for minimization, 
Minimization of product of sum and sum of product forms, Incompletely specified functions, Multiple 
output circuits, Quine McClusky method for minimization 
Introduction to HDL: Typical VLSI design flow, Emergence of HDLs, Importance of HDLs, 
Hierarchical modeling concepts, Modules, Instances, Lexical conventions, Data types 
Gate Level Modeling: Gate types, Gate delays, Design examples 
Laboratory Components: 
1. Introduction to Digital ICs, Verification of logic gates, Verification of simple Boolean expression 
using discrete components 
Module 2: Design and Realization of Combinational Circuits No. of Hrs: 09 + 04 
Combinational Circuit Design: Introduction to signed arithmetic, Adders, Subtractors, Ripple carry 
adder, Fast adders, Multiplexers, Decoders, Encoders, Implementation of logic functions using 
Multiplexers and Decoders, Code converters, Magnitude comparators 
Modules & Ports: Definitions, Port connection rules, Port connection types with examples 
Data Flow Modeling:  Continuous assignments, Expressions, Operators, Operands, Time delay 
specifications, Examples 
Laboratory Components: 
1. To realize Adder/Subtractors circuits using Verilog HDL at gate level 
2. To realize 4-bit Ripple carry adder in gate level and data flow style modeling 
Module 3: Sequential Circuit Fundamentals No. of Hrs: 10 + 04 
Sequential circuit building blocks: Basic latch, Gated SR latch, Gated D latch, Master slave and edge 
triggered, D flip flops, T flip flop, JK flip flop, Registers, Asynchronous counters, Synchronous 
counters, Ring counter and Johnson counter. 
Behavioral Modeling : Structured procedures, Procedural assignments, Conditional statements, 
Multiway branching, Loops.

Network Analysis and Synthesis 
Semester III CIE Marks 50 
Course Code 23ECPC205 SEE Marks 50 
Teaching Hrs/Week (L: T: P) 2:2:0 Exam Hrs 03 
Total Hrs 42 Credits 03 
Course Learning Objectives: This course is designed to 
1. Familiarize the application of network reduction techniques, mesh/nodal analysis, network 
theorems, resonance and Laplace Transform 
2. Develop the ability to analyze and synthesize a given DC or AC circuit 
Module 1: Network Reduction and Analysis Methods No. of Hrs: 05+04 
Network elements, Types of sources, Source transformation , Source Shifting, Star-Delta 
transformation, Mesh current analysis, Node voltage analysis, Concept of Super mesh and 
Supernode applied for DC and AC networks 
Module 2: Network Theorems No. of Hrs: 04+04 
Superposition theorem, Millman's theorem, Thevenin's and Norton 's theorems, Maximum power 
transfer theorem 
Module 3: Transient Analysis No. of Hrs: 04+04 
Behavior of circuit elements under switching condition and their representation, Evaluation of initial 
and final conditions in RL, RC and RLC circuits for AC and DC excitations 
Introduction to Laplace Transform, Solution of networks using Laplace Transform 
Module 4: Two port networks and Resonance No. of Hrs: 04+04 
Definition of Impedance (Z), Admittance (Y), hybrid (h) and Transmission (T) parameters, 
Relationship between parameter sets, Reciprocal and Symmetrical networks 
Series Resonance: Resonant frequency, Selectivity and Bandwidth, Q-Factor 
Parallel Resonance: Practical parallel resonant circuit, Parallel resonant circuit with resistance 
present in both branches 
Module 5: Network Synthesis No. of Hrs: 04+05 
Network function, Hurwitz Polynomial, Positive real function, Synthesis of LC, RC and RL 
networks using Foster forms and Cauer forms 
Course Outcomes: At the end of the course, the student will be able to 
1. Understand the basic concepts of network analysis and synthesis techniques 
2. Solve the given circuit with DC or AC excitation using network theorems and Laplace Transform 
3. Analyze the given electrical network in time and frequency domain 
4. Synthesize one port network using Foster and Cauer forms

Internship refers to the position of a student as trainee or a temporary (or unconfirmed)

experience or satisfy requirements for a qualification. It is a structured,  supervised 
professional experience in an industry, research organization, or incubation centers  
Internships play a vital role in bridging the gap between theoretical education and professional 
practice. In general, engineering internships serve as a crucial component of professional 
education by providing experiential learning, industry readiness, an d holistic skill 
development, ultimately producing competent engineers or entrepreneurs. Apart from these, 
it develops professional ethics, work culture awareness and communication skills 
 
Types of Internships: 
Following are the types of internships:  
i. Industry Internship : Carried out in the engineering industry, companies, 
manufacturing units, startups, business, IT industry. The topic involved may be 
technical, managerial, production -related tasks, live projects, or innovative 
activities 
ii. Research Internship : Carried out at universities, research labs, or R&D 
departments or organizations. The internship involves literature review, data 
analysis, and experimental work leading to publications, prototypes, technical 
reports or innovations. The research internshi p may induce students to plan for 
higher studies or academic careers 
iii. Entrepreneurship Internship : Undertaken in association with start -ups, or 
entrepreneurship cells or launching own idea in Preincubation/Incubation centers.
